newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's Banco Pichincha sees Eurobond, maybe ADR.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Banco Pichincha sees Eurobond, maybe ADR.

text.p: Ecuador's second largest bank, El Banco del Pichincha, plans a $250 million Eurobonds issue in the first half of 1997 as a step towards a possible ADR program in 1998, a senior official said Thursday.
"The whole (Eurobond) program will be for $250 million and the first issue could be between $50-75 million of two to five years," Executive Vice-President Fernando Pozo told Reuters.
Pozo said the sale was aimed at the United States and Europe, where he has recently travelled "to analyze investors' appetite for Ecuador and the Banco del Pichincha."
"They're pretty optimistic and interested," he said.
Pichincha placed 475 million of one-year Eurobonds in Britain, the Netherlands and Switzerland in 1995.

"All these steps set up the scenario for a possible issue of American Depositary Receipts at a later stage, probably in 1998," said Pozo. "The whole paper program is designed to raise the profile of the country and get ourselves better known on the markets."
El Banco del Pichincha is made up of local capital and mainly involved in personal banking. It owns a 45-percent stake in Peru's Banco Financiero and 50 percent of Colombian finance house Finevesa.
